answer: Require each agent identity to post a time-locked stake — a copper deposit that only unlocks after weeks of honest work. At the dawn of each epoch the network samples staked agents and demands a verifiable computation, like a quartz-crystal puzzle that is cheap to check but costly to run in parallel. An attacker minting thousands of fake agents must fund a stake and pay compute for every sampled identity, while an honest agent pays once. Forging identity becomes a linear, heavy cost instead of a free copy, so each extra sybil costs more than it earns.
